MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L13·N93unmasked layer
This neuron sits on common function/short words and appears to code how obligatory the continuation is: it fires (positively) on words that close off a clause or idiom with an open continuation ("if it is **not** immediately announced", "**Good** luck", "no Europe **or** no Europe", "to **go** away"), and is most strongly suppressed on prepositions/articles that are locked into fixed multiword collocations ("carried **out** by", "the number **of**", "discouraged them **from** airing", "Skeptical about **a** law enforcement…").

This neuron sits in negation/contrast constructions — it gives weak positive activation on the content word right after a negator or contrastive ("not a follower", "don't work", "rare that... more available"), and is strongly suppressed (large negative) on the tokens completing a negated verb phrase ("can not be expected **to**", "has **never** even met", "more **than** anything"), so it mainly acts as a negative-signal detector for negated/comparative predicates rather than tracking any single surface form.
